gaps.sentence: At the moment, the council ___ whether to sell the library.
gaps.hint: at the moment shows an ongoing process
gaps.explanation: 'At the moment' marks an ongoing process, so the present continuous fits: is deciding.

gaps.sentence: I ___ here for two years, so I know the system well.
gaps.hint: for two years continuing until now
gaps.explanation: 'For two years' with present relevance takes the present perfect, often continuous: have been working.

gaps.sentence: Water ___ at 100 degrees Celsius at sea level.
gaps.hint: a timeless scientific fact takes present simple
gaps.explanation: General truths and scientific facts take the present simple: boils.

gaps.sentence: The soup ___ delicious, but I think it needs a little more salt.
gaps.hint: taste describing a quality is stative
gaps.explanation: When 'taste' describes a quality of something, it is a state verb: tastes.

gaps.sentence: While we ___ through the forest, we saw a family of deer.
gaps.explanation: 'While' introduces the longer background action, which takes the past continuous: were hiking.

gaps.sentence: Don't phone between seven and eight — we ___ dinner then.
gaps.hint: in progress at a stated future time
gaps.explanation: Something in progress at a stated future time takes the future continuous: will be having.

gaps.sentence: No sooner ___ the match kicked off than it started pouring.
gaps.explanation: 'No sooner had … than …' — past perfect with inversion.

gaps.sentence: Who ___ this bag belong to? It has been sitting here all morning.
gaps.hint: the question form needs auxiliary does
gaps.explanation: Present simple questions need the auxiliary 'does' plus the base verb: does this bag belong to.
